authority: Canonical operational field-battle day/contact lifecycle. Exact casualties remain battle_resolve authority; operational battlefield state owns day/night posture and intervention boundaries.

operational_contact.rule: One operational battle_resolve settles one bounded contact period, never an entire persistent battlefield. Daylight contact stops at sunset. A new organized night contact is lawful only when every attacking formation already carries a saved aggressive operational order. Night does not inherit automatic contact merely because the formations attacked during the day. Registered military/autonomy scheduler boundaries can end a contact period early so reinforcement, interception, command, convoy and campaign movement work settles before the next contact.

night_camp.rule: At dusk an active operational battlefield enters sector-local camp/security posture without teleporting formations or erasing geometry. Ambient combat pressure stops and can recover except in a sector with an explicitly active night contact. At dawn only formations recorded as having actually camped through the preceding night may receive ordinary idle-fatigue recovery and refit from physical ammunition, spare outfitting sets and remount horses already in custody. Casualties, wounds and destroyed material never reset.

reserve_terms.tactical_reserve: A persistent formation deliberately withheld from direct contact inside the operational battlefield.
reserve_terms.relief: A combat formation or 100-man echelon temporarily replaces another frontage element.
reserve_terms.sustainment_rotation: A bounded 100-man command-echelon task for rearm, remount, refit or rest; it does not create a new reserve formation.
reserve_terms.command_rear: The battlefield HQ/baggage area that physically holds command and nearby formation support stock.
reserve_terms.field_camp: The overnight or extended-rest posture inside controlled battlefield space; it does not imply a strategic location change.
reserve_terms.strategic_reserve: A separate formation or army not yet committed to the operational battlefield/contact.

invariants: Operational contact periods advance real campaign chronology so redeployments, reinforcements, reports and autonomous actors can intervene between contacts.
A local contact winner is not automatically the winner of the persistent battle.

Field battle uses the canonical derived strategic-supply condition. Combat never consumes a formation ration or animal-feed inventory because ordinary field subsistence is not a persistent formation asset.
No camp, dawn or sustainment transition creates ammunition, equipment, horses, personnel or recovered casualties.
Dusk and dawn change battlefield posture, not strategic location or sovereignty.
Only formations recorded in the preceding dusk camp roster receive dawn camp refit; a late-arriving reinforcement cannot receive a full night of recovery it did not experience.
An explicit night contact suppresses night-camp pressure recovery only in its exact sector and only for its saved contact window.

Registered military/autonomy scheduler events may truncate a contact period before casualties are settled past the event, allowing external armies and support work to intervene causally between contacts.
